questions.question: Which planet in our solar system is closest to the Sun?
questions.funFact: Mercury has almost no air, so its days are scorching and its nights are freezing.

questions.question: What is the name of the galaxy that contains our solar system?
questions.funFact: From inside, we see our galaxy as a faint, milky band of stars across the night sky.

questions.question: Which planet is famous for its bright, wide rings?
questions.funFact: Saturn is so light for its size that it is less dense than water.

questions.question: What is the name of Earth's only natural satellite?
questions.funFact: The Moon drifts about four centimeters farther from Earth every year.

questions.question: Who was the first human to travel into space?
questions.funFact: His orbit around Earth in 1961 lasted only about one hour and forty-eight minutes.

questions.question: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
questions.funFact: Mars looks red because its dusty surface contains lots of rust, or iron oxide.

questions.question: Which planet spins on its side, rolling around the Sun like a ball?
questions.funFact: Its poles each get about forty-two years of sunlight, then forty-two years of darkness.

questions.question: Which planet is the hottest in our solar system?
questions.funFact: Venus is hotter than Mercury because its thick carbon dioxide air traps heat.

questions.question: Which mission first landed humans on the Moon in 1969?
questions.funFact: Two astronauts walked on the Moon's surface for about two and a half hours.
